concepts.title: Respiratory Organs and the Human Respiratory System

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Respiratory Organs and the Human Respiratory System' refers to.
questions.a: Respiration occurs through body surface, tracheal system, gills or lungs depending on the animal; the human respiratory system includes external nostrils, nasal passage, pharynx, larynx with sound box, trachea, bronchi, bronchioles and alveoli surrounded by blood capillaries, with the lungs covered by pleural membranes.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Respiratory Organs and the Human Respiratory System'.
questions.a: The alveoli, with their thin squamous epithelium and dense capillary network, are the primary sites of exchange of gases, while the conducting part only transports the air.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Respiratory Organs and the Human Respiratory System' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 14.1 Respiratory Organs, 14.2 Human Respiratory System (source: kebo114.txt sections 14.1, 14.2)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Exchange and Transport of Gases' refers to.
questions.a: Oxygen and carbon dioxide exchange by pressure gradient across alveolar and tissue membranes; oxygen is transported mainly as oxyhaemoglobin, carbon dioxide mostly as bicarbonate formed under the enzyme carbonic anhydrase, and every 100 ml of deoxygenated blood delivers about 4 ml of carbon dioxide to the alveoli.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Exchange and Transport of Gases'.
questions.a: The oxygen dissociation curve is sigmoid, and its shift to the right with higher carbon dioxide, hydrogen ion and temperature is the Bohr effect that favours unloading in tissues.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Exchange and Transport of Gases' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 14.4 Exchange of Gases, 14.5 Transport of Gases (source: kebo114.txt sections 14.4, 14.5)

concepts.title: Regulation of Respiration and Respiratory Disorders

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Regulation of Respiration and Respiratory Disorders' refers to.
questions.a: Breathing is regulated by the respiratory rhythm centre in the medulla, the pneumotaxic centre in the pons and chemosensitive areas sensing carbon dioxide and hydrogen ions; disorders include asthma with bronchial constriction, emphysema with alveolar damage, and occupational respiratory disorders like asbestosis and silicosis.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Regulation of Respiration and Respiratory Disorders'.
questions.a: Carbon dioxide acts as the major stimulus for breathing through chemosensors, since oxygen plays only a minor role in normal regulation.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Regulation of Respiration and Respiratory Disorders' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 14.6 Regulation of Respiration, 14.7 Disorders of Respiratory System (source: kebo114.txt sections 14.6, 14.7)
